purpose: cjson is a lightweight C library for parsing and generating JSON.

functions.cJSON_Minify: `cJSON_Minify` edits a writable JSON string in place to remove whitespace and C-style comments. Use it on a mutable buffer only; `NULL` is ignored. It skips spaces, tabs, CR/LF, `//` and `/* */`, compacting the text.
functions.cJSON_CreateBool: Creates a new cJSON value of type boolean. Pass a `cJSON_bool`; nonzero becomes `cJSON_True`, zero becomes `cJSON_False`. Returns a newly allocated `cJSON*`, or `NULL` if allocation fails.
functions.cJSON_CreateNull:
`cJSON_CreateNull()` creates a new cJSON item representing JSON `null`. Use it when building a JSON tree and you need a null value. It allocates a fresh item; on success `type` is set to `cJSON_NULL`, otherwise it returns `NULL`.
This is a misuse of ownership semantics, not a bug in cJSON_CreateNull itself. cJSON_CreateNull only allocates and returns a new cJSON node; the caller owns it until a container insertion succeeds. After creating an item with cJSON_CreateNull, always check the return value for NULL, then pass it to cJSON_InsertItemInArray/cJSON_AddItemToArray only with valid target containers and indexes. Most importantly, if the insertion call returns false, immediately release the item with cJSON_Delete(item) because ownership was not transferred. Do not assume creation implies automatic cleanup by the library.
functions.cJSON_PrintBuffered: `cJSON_PrintBuffered` renders a cJSON tree to text with a preallocated buffer. Use it when you can estimate output size to reduce reallocations. `prebuffer < 0` or alloc failure returns `NULL`; on print failure it frees the buffer and returns `NULL`. `fmt` selects formatted/unformatted output.
functions.cJSON_IsString: `cJSON_IsString` is a type-check helper. Use it to test whether a `cJSON*` is a string item. It returns `false` for `NULL`, otherwise `true` only when `(item->type & 0xFF) == cJSON_String`; it doesn’t inspect the string contents.
functions.cJSON_Delete: Frees a cJSON node and its owned descendants. Call it on a parsed/created item when done. It walks `next` siblings, recursively deletes `child`, and frees `valuestring`/`string` only if not marked `cJSON_IsReference`/`cJSON_StringIsConst`.
functions.cJSON_Duplicate: `cJSON_Duplicate` creates a copy of a `cJSON` item. Use it on an existing item; `recurse=0` duplicates only the node, `recurse=1` duplicates the whole subtree. If `item` is `NULL`, it returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_GetObjectItemCaseSensitive: Returns the child item in a JSON object whose key exactly matches `string` (case-sensitive). Use it on a `cJSON` object node, not arrays/primitives. If `object`/`string` is NULL or no exact match exists, it returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_AddNumberToObject: Adds a numeric child to a cJSON object. Use it with a valid `object`, key `name`, and `double` value. It creates a number item, inserts it, and returns that item on success; on failure it deletes the item and returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_GetArraySize: `cJSON_GetArraySize` counts linked `child` nodes and returns the number of items in an array or object. Use it on a valid `cJSON*`; if `array == NULL`, it returns 0. It walks all children, so size is O(n), and the `int` return can overflow for huge inputs.
functions.cJSON_DeleteItemFromObjectCaseSensitive: Deletes a case-sensitive object member by key. Use it on a cJSON object and a key string; it detaches the matching item, then frees it via `cJSON_Delete`. If no match is found, nothing is deleted.
functions.cJSON_CreateObject: `cJSON_CreateObject()` allocates a new empty `cJSON` item and sets its type to `cJSON_Object`. Use it to start building a JSON object, then add members with cJSON add-item APIs. If allocation fails, it returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_CreateDoubleArray: Creates a JSON array from a `double` C array. Use with a non-NULL `numbers` pointer and `count >= 0`. Returns `NULL` on invalid input or allocation failure; otherwise builds an array of number items, deleting partial results if creation fails.
functions.cJSON_AddNullToObject: `cJSON_AddNullToObject` creates a JSON null item and adds it to the given object under `name`. Use it when you want to set an object member to `null`. On success it returns the new item; on failure it deletes it and returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_IsNumber: `cJSON_IsNumber` checks whether a `cJSON` item is a number. Use it on a non-NULL `cJSON*`; it returns `true` only when the item exists and its low 8 bits of `type` equal `cJSON_Number`, otherwise `false`.
functions.cJSON_AddRawToObject: Adds a raw JSON fragment as a named member of an object. Use it with a valid object, key, and raw JSON text. It creates a raw item, inserts it, returns the item on success, or `NULL` if creation/insertion fails.
functions.cJSON_AddItemToArray: `cJSON_AddItemToArray` appends an existing `cJSON` item to an array (and is also used for object-linked lists internally). Pass a valid array/object and a non-NULL item. It returns `true` on success, `false` if inputs are invalid or insertion fails.
functions.cJSON_AddStringToObject: Adds a JSON string member to an object. Use with a valid `cJSON` object, key `name`, and C string `string`. It creates a string item, inserts it, and returns the new item. On failure, it deletes the item and returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_malloc: `cJSON_malloc` is a thin wrapper around the allocator set by `cJSON_InitHooks`. Use it when you need cJSON’s configured `malloc` behavior. It simply calls `global_hooks.allocate(size)` and returns that result, so it depends entirely on the current hook setup.
functions.cJSON_SetValuestring: `cJSON_SetValuestring` updates the `valuestring` of a non-reference `cJSON_String` item. Use it only on valid string nodes with non-NULL strings. It returns the stored string on success, or `NULL` if type/refs are wrong, input is NULL, corrupted, or overlap makes `strcpy` unsafe.
functions.cJSON_CreateFalse: Creates a new cJSON value representing JSON `false`. Use it when building a JSON tree and you need a boolean false node. Returns a newly allocated `cJSON*` with type set to `cJSON_False`, or `NULL` if allocation fails.
functions.cJSON_GetErrorPtr: `cJSON_GetErrorPtr()` returns a pointer into the last failed `cJSON_Parse()` input at the parse error position. Use it after a parse failure to inspect nearby text; it returns `0`/NULL when parsing succeeds.
functions.cJSON_IsNull: `cJSON_IsNull` checks whether a `cJSON` item is the JSON `null` type. Use it on a `cJSON*`; it returns `false` for `NULL` pointers and `true` only when `item->type & 0xFF` equals `cJSON_NULL`.
functions.cJSON_AddItemToObject: Adds `item` to a JSON object under key `string`. Use it with a valid object and owned `cJSON*` item. It returns `cJSON_bool` from the internal add routine: success on valid inputs, failure if the object/item/key can’t be added.
functions.cJSON_ReplaceItemViaPointer: Replaces `item` in `parent` with `replacement` using pointers, preserving list links and shifting later items right. Use only with items already in `parent`. Returns false on NULL args; true if `replacement==item`; updates `parent->child` when replacing the first item.
functions.cJSON_ReplaceItemInArray: Replaces the array element at index `which` with `newitem`. Use only with a valid `cJSON` array and nonnegative index. If `which < 0`, it returns `false`; otherwise it looks up that item and delegates to pointer-based replacement.
functions.cJSON_CreateRaw: Creates a `cJSON_Raw` item holding a copied raw JSON text string. Use it when you want cJSON to store/print preformatted JSON without parsing it. If allocation or string copy fails, it deletes the item and returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_HasObjectItem: `cJSON_HasObjectItem` is a convenience check for object membership. Pass a cJSON object and a key string; it returns `1` if `cJSON_GetObjectItem` finds a matching item, otherwise `0`. Use it when you only need existence, not the value.
functions.cJSON_GetObjectItem: `cJSON_GetObjectItem` fetches a child item from a JSON object by key, using case-insensitive matching. Pass an object node and the key string; it returns the matching `cJSON*` or `NULL` if the object/key is invalid or not found.
functions.cJSON_CreateStringReference: Creates a cJSON string node that **references** external memory. Use it when the string is managed elsewhere and must **not** be freed by `cJSON_Delete`. If allocation fails, returns `NULL`. The input may be `NULL`; then `valuestring` is set to `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_CreateString: Creates a new `cJSON` string item from a C string. Use it to build JSON values, then add/attach the returned item to an array/object. If allocation or string duplication fails, it deletes the item and returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_Parse: `cJSON_Parse` is a simple wrapper for `cJSON_ParseWithOpts(value, 0, 0)`. Use it to parse a JSON string into a `cJSON*` tree. On success, free with `cJSON_Delete`; on parse failure, it returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_PrintUnformatted: `cJSON_PrintUnformatted` serializes a `cJSON` item to compact JSON text with no whitespace/pretty-printing. Use it when you need transfer/storage output. It returns a newly allocated `char*` (or `NULL` on failure); free it with cJSON’s free hook.
functions.cJSON_SetNumberHelper: Helper for `cJSON_SetNumberValue`: set a cJSON number’s `valueint` and `valuedouble`. Use it on a number item. It clamps `valueint` to `INT_MAX/INT_MIN` when out of range, otherwise casts to `int`, and returns the stored `valuedouble`.
functions.cJSON_ParseWithLengthOpts: Parses JSON from a buffer with an explicit length. Use it when input may not be NUL-terminated; `return_parse_end` gets the stop position. Fails on `NULL`/0 length or parse errors, and can require the input to end exactly at the JSON text.
functions.cJSON_AddArrayToObject: Creates a new empty JSON array and adds it to `object` under `name`. Use it for object members meant to hold arrays. On success returns the new array; on failure returns `NULL` and deletes the created array.
functions.cJSON_DeleteItemFromObject: `cJSON_DeleteItemFromObject` removes an item from a JSON object by key and frees it. Use it on an object plus a member name. If the key exists, it’s detached then deleted; if not, nothing is deleted.
functions.cJSON_PrintPreallocated: `cJSON_PrintPreallocated` renders a `cJSON` value into a caller-provided buffer, avoiding internal allocation. Use it with a valid `buffer` and nonnegative `length`; `format` controls pretty-printing. It returns `1` on success, `0` if args are invalid or output doesn't fit.
functions.cJSON_AddItemToObjectCS: Adds `item` to `object` using a const key string. Use only for literals/long-lived strings; cJSON won’t copy/free the key and marks it const. Returns true/false via `add_item_to_object`; behavior depends on object/item validity and allocation success.
functions.cJSON_IsRaw: `cJSON_IsRaw` checks whether a `cJSON` item is a Raw node. Use it to test an item before treating it as raw JSON text. It returns `false` for `NULL`, otherwise `true` only when `(item->type & 0xFF) == cJSON_Raw`.
functions.cJSON_InsertItemInArray: Inserts `newitem` into `array` at index `which`. Use with a valid array and non-NULL item; negative index fails. If `which` is past the end, it appends. It also rejects corrupted list links.
functions.cJSON_Print: `cJSON_Print` renders a `cJSON` item into a newly allocated, formatted JSON text string using the global hooks. Use it to serialize a parsed/constructed tree for storage/transfer. It returns `NULL` on failure; free the result with the matching cJSON deallocator.
functions.cJSON_CreateStringArray: Creates a cJSON array from `count` C strings. Use with a non-NULL `strings` pointer and `count >= 0`. Returns NULL if args are invalid, allocation fails, or any element creation fails; on failure it deletes the partially built array.
functions.cJSON_CreateTrue: `cJSON_CreateTrue()` creates a new cJSON boolean item set to JSON `true`. Use it when building a JSON tree and you need a true literal. It allocates a new node; returns `NULL` if allocation fails.
functions.cJSON_Version: Returns cJSON’s version as a static string like `major.minor.patch`. Call it with no args to query the library version; the returned pointer stays valid, but the buffer is reused on each call.
functions.cJSON_CreateIntArray: Creates a JSON array from `count` ints. Use with a valid `numbers` pointer and `count >= 0`; `count` must not exceed the source array length. Returns `NULL` on invalid args or allocation failure, and deletes the partially built array on failure.
functions.cJSON_CreateArrayReference: Creates a cJSON array node that **references** an existing child list, not a copy. Use it when you want to wrap already-built items as an array without duplicating them. If allocation fails, returns `NULL`. The referenced child is cast away from `const`.
functions.cJSON_ParseWithLength: `cJSON_ParseWithLength` is a convenience wrapper for parsing JSON from a buffer with a known length. Use it when the input may not be NUL-terminated. It simply calls `cJSON_ParseWithLengthOpts(value, buffer_length, 0, 0)`, so it parses the whole buffer and provides no return-parse-end info.
functions.cJSON_IsFalse: `cJSON_IsFalse` checks whether a `cJSON` item is the JSON boolean false. Use it on a `cJSON*` to test type safely. It returns `false` if `item == NULL`, otherwise `true` only when `(item->type & 0xFF) == cJSON_False`.
functions.cJSON_AddBoolToObject: Creates a JSON boolean child and adds it to an object under `name`. Use it with a valid object; it returns the new item on success. If insertion fails, it deletes the created bool and returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_IsObject: `cJSON_IsObject` checks whether a `cJSON*` is a non-NULL JSON object. Use it before treating `item` as an object. It returns `false` for `NULL` or any non-object type, and `true` only when `(item->type & 0xFF) == cJSON_Object`.
functions.cJSON_DetachItemViaPointer: Detaches `item` from `parent`’s array/object without deleting it. Use only with a direct child of `parent`; returns `NULL` for NULL args or if `item` isn’t linked to `parent`. On success, links are fixed and the item is left standalone.
functions.cJSON_IsBool: `cJSON_IsBool` checks whether a `cJSON` item is a boolean (`true` or `false`). Use it to test an item before reading it as a bool. It returns `false` for `NULL` and for non-bool types; otherwise `true` if `type` has `cJSON_True` or `cJSON_False`.
functions.cJSON_free: `cJSON_free` releases memory using cJSON’s configured deallocator (`global_hooks.deallocate`). Use it to free memory allocated by cJSON or via its hooks. It safely accepts `NULL` if the deallocator does. Setting `object = NULL` only affects the local copy.
functions.cJSON_IsInvalid: `cJSON_IsInvalid` checks whether a `cJSON` item’s base type is `cJSON_Invalid`. Use it to test an item before other operations. It returns `false` for `NULL`, and `true` only when `(item->type & 0xFF) == cJSON_Invalid`.
functions.cJSON_AddTrueToObject: Adds a boolean `true` item to a JSON object under `name`. Use it on an object created by cJSON; it returns the new item on success, or `NULL` if insertion fails, deleting the created item.
functions.cJSON_DetachItemFromArray: Detaches and returns the item at index `which` from a cJSON array without deleting it. Use with `which >= 0`; negative returns `NULL`. If the index is invalid/out of range, behavior depends on `get_array_item` via `NULL` result.
functions.cJSON_Compare: `cJSON_Compare` recursively tests two cJSON values for equality. Use it to compare parsed/constructed JSON trees, optionally case-sensitive for object keys. It returns false if either input is NULL/invalid, types differ, or types are unsupported; identical pointers are true.
functions.cJSON_DetachItemFromObjectCaseSensitive: Detaches and returns the object member matching `string` with case-sensitive lookup. Use on a JSON object to remove an item without deleting it. If `object`/key is invalid or not found, it returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_CreateObjectReference: Creates a reference wrapper for an existing cJSON object/array. Use it when you want to reuse `child` without transferring ownership. `cJSON_Delete` won’t free the referenced elements. Returns `NULL` on allocation failure.
functions.cJSON_GetArrayItem: `cJSON_GetArrayItem` fetches the element at a zero-based index from a cJSON array. Use it with a valid array and nonnegative index. If `index < 0`, or the item can’t be found, it returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_DeleteItemFromArray: Deletes the array element at index `which` from `array`. It first detaches that item, then frees it with `cJSON_Delete`. Use on a valid cJSON array; if the index is out of range or the array is invalid, nothing is deleted.
functions.cJSON_AddItemReferenceToArray: Adds a reference to an existing item into an array without transferring ownership. Use it to reuse a cJSON node safely. If `array` is `NULL`, it returns `false`; otherwise it appends a reference wrapper and returns the result.
functions.cJSON_InitHooks: Sets cJSON’s global memory hooks. Call before creating/parsing JSON. `NULL` resets to `malloc/free/realloc`. Custom `malloc_fn`/`free_fn` override defaults; `realloc` is enabled only when both remain the standard `malloc` and `free`.
functions.cJSON_DetachItemFromObject: Detaches and returns the object member with the given key. Use it on an object and a key string; the item is removed from the object but not freed, so you own the returned cJSON. If the key isn’t found, it returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_AddItemReferenceToObject: Adds a key/value to a JSON object by **reference**: it creates a reference wrapper for `item` and inserts it under `string`. Use it when you want to reuse an existing cJSON node without transferring ownership. Returns false if `object` or `string` is NULL.
functions.cJSON_GetStringValue: `cJSON_GetStringValue` is a safe accessor for string items. Use it on a `cJSON*` to get `valuestring` only if the item is a JSON string; otherwise it returns `NULL`. It does not copy or convert data.
functions.cJSON_ReplaceItemInObjectCaseSensitive: Replaces an object member by key using a case-sensitive match. Use with a cJSON object, the target key, and a new item. Returns true on success; false if the object/key is invalid or the member isn’t found.
functions.cJSON_ReplaceItemInObject: `cJSON_ReplaceItemInObject` replaces an object member by key with `newitem` without case-insensitive matching. Use it on a `cJSON` object and a valid key; it returns true on success, false if the key/object isn’t found or inputs are invalid.
functions.cJSON_CreateNumber: Creates a new cJSON number item. Use it to build JSON numeric values. It allocates a cJSON node, sets type to `cJSON_Number`, stores `valuedouble=num`, and sets `valueint` with saturation to `INT_MAX/INT_MIN` on overflow; returns `NULL` if allocation fails.
functions.cJSON_ParseWithOpts: `cJSON_ParseWithOpts` is a thin wrapper around `cJSON_ParseWithLengthOpts`. It parses a NUL-terminated JSON string, optionally requiring full NUL termination. Use `return_parse_end` to get the parse end or error position; on `NULL` input it returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_IsTrue: `cJSON_IsTrue` checks whether a `cJSON` item is the JSON boolean true. Use it on a `cJSON*` after parsing or creation. It returns `false` for `NULL` and for any item whose type isn’t `cJSON_True`.
functions.cJSON_IsArray: `cJSON_IsArray` checks whether a `cJSON*` is a non-NULL array item. Use it before treating `item` as an array. It returns `false` for `NULL` or any non-array type, and `true` only when `(item->type & 0xFF) == cJSON_Array`.
functions.cJSON_GetNumberValue: `cJSON_GetNumberValue` safely reads a `cJSON` number as `double`. Use it only on numeric items; otherwise it returns `NAN`. It does not convert other types or report errors beyond that.
functions.cJSON_AddObjectToObject: Creates a new empty cJSON object and adds it to `object` under `name`. Use it to build nested objects. On success it returns the new child object; on failure it deletes it and returns NULL.
functions.cJSON_AddFalseToObject: `cJSON_AddFalseToObject` creates a JSON `false` item and adds it to an object under `name`. Use it for boolean false members. On success it returns the new item; on failure it deletes it and returns `NULL` (e.g., invalid object/name or add failure).
functions.cJSON_CreateArray: Creates a new empty `cJSON` array node. Use it when building JSON arrays manually, then add elements with cJSON_AddItemToArray. Returns a newly allocated array item, or `NULL` if allocation fails.
functions.cJSON_CreateFloatArray: Creates a JSON array from a float buffer. Use with a non-NULL `numbers` and `count >= 0`; it returns `NULL` on invalid input or allocation failure. Each float is converted to a JSON number, and the whole array is deleted if any element creation fails.
